verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Floating in the Pacific Ocean on Friday... waters off San Diego" (R1); "off the coast of San Diego" (R2, R3, R4, R6, R7); "Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego" (R3); "Pacific Ocean just after 8 p.m. Eastern" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission splashed down at 8:07 p.m. EDT on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "at 8:07 p.m. Eastern time" (R1); "8:07 p.m. EDT" (R2, R4); "8:07 p.m. ET" (R3, R6, R7); "just after 8 p.m. Eastern on Friday" (R5); date confirmed as April 10, 2026 across sources
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm the exact time and date in EDT/ET.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission splashed down at 5:07 p.m. PDT on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)" (R2); "5:07 p.m. local time" (R3); "8:07 p.m. ET Friday, April 10, 2026" equivalent to 5:07 p.m. PDT (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state or equivalently confirm 5:07 p.m. PDT on the specified date.

verifications.claim: The splashdown location was the Pacific Ocean west of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Pacific Ocean... waters off San Diego" (R1); "off the coast of San Diego" (R2, R3, R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Pacific Ocean off San Diego coast; 'west' is precise as San Diego faces Pacific to the west.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule carried four astronauts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "four astronauts" (R1, R3); "The Artemis II crew — NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen" (R2); lists four (R6, R7)
verifications.reasoning: All sources consistently name or state four astronauts aboard Orion.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule returned after a 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "10-day mission" (R3); "10-day journey around the moon" (R6); launch April 1 to splashdown April 10 (R1)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly describe it as a 10-day mission.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule's reentry occurred at approximately 24,000 miles per hour.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "more than 24,000 miles per hour"; "peak velocity of 24,664 miles per hour" (R1); "peak velocity of 24,664 mph" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state reentry/peak velocity at or above 24,000 mph, matching approximately.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission lasted over 9 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Launch April 1 to splashdown April 10 (R1); "10-day mission" (R3, R6)
verifications.reasoning: Mission duration from April 1-10 exceeds 9 days, explicitly called 10 days.

verifications.claim: Recovery teams were on-site immediately to secure the capsule and assist the crew, as shown on Fox News and reported by Florida Today.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "took more than an hour to approach the bobbing capsule" (R1); "Within two hours after splashdown" (R2); "recovery forces were seen approaching after splashdown" (R3, Fox News); recovery process described but not immediate (R6, Florida Today)
verifications.reasoning: Sources (including cited Fox R3 and Florida Today R6) describe recovery starting soon but explicitly note it took over an hour or up to two hours, contradicting 'immediately'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission was the first crewed mission to the Moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first people to leave low-Earth orbit since 1972" (R1); "first humans toward the Moon since 1972" (R2); "first crewed mission beyond low Earth orbit since 1972" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm first crewed deep space/Moon mission since 1972 (over 50 years to 2026).
